source.title: Reconstructing Training Data from Trained Neural Networks
source.authors: Niv Haim; Gal Vardi; Gilad Yehudai; Ohad Shamir; M. Irani

record.tranche_reason: Reports training and test performance for naturally labeled classifiers, bearing on the natural-label generalization part of V1, but does not test random-label fitting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports zero training error and test accuracy for natural-label binary classifiers. It does not train on random labels or compare conditions from V2–V8.
record.test_reason: The study measures reconstruction of training inputs from classifier parameters. Its natural-label training and test accuracies do not test V1's coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization: no random-label models are trained. Reconstruction is also different from V8's label-influence measure and example-removal experiment. No results establish the comparisons specified in V2–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: in some relatively small binary MLP settings, trained classifier parameters contain enough information to reconstruct a substantial portion of training inputs. The authors demonstrate a reconstruction scheme motivated by implicit-bias results and identify scaling to convolutional networks, larger datasets, and other domains as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains binary MLP classifiers and evaluates reconstruction of their training samples; it does not test random-label memorization or the claim's mapped generalization conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-set size and architecture vary in the CIFAR10 comparisons; the authors state that adding training samples improves test accuracy while adding layers keeps test accuracy approximately the same.

fits_no_version.finding: Binary MLPs attain zero training error and 72%–79% CIFAR10 test accuracy; the main MNIST model attains 88.0%. Both tasks have balanced classes, giving a 50% chance baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These natural-label binary classifiers interpolate their training sets while retaining above-chance held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed reconstruction method recovers recognizable training inputs from trained binary MLP parameters, particularly inputs near the classification margin.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-input recoverability can coexist with above-chance classifier generalization; this does not establish random-label fitting or the accuracy cost of removing influential examples.

record.code_released: The authors state: “We will release the code.” Project page: https://giladude1.github.io/reconstruction
record.problems: The study does not test random labels. The reported natural-label results are binary MLPs on MNIST and CIFAR10, so they do not establish the full V1 conjunction. No error bars are reported; the checklist marks error bars N/A.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and their coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
The trajectory of test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets.
A batch-size generalization penalty beyond a workload-dependent threshold and its recovery through recipe changes; the supplementary SGD reconstruction experiment does not establish this.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Label memorization measured through inclusion influence, followed by removal and retraining against a random-removal control.

record.verdict_notes: The row states indicate inability to determine a claim-version effect, not an error in the reported test accuracies. Reconstruction findings and supplementary classifier accuracies fall outside the supplied versions, so their omission is not a missing claim-bearing result.

versions.untested_parts: Whether these same architectures and recipes fit random labels, and whether test accuracy on random labels stays at chance.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Natural-label binary MLPs on MNIST and CIFAR10 in the reported settings
reader_labels.reason: The models achieve zero training error and report test accuracies of 88.0% and 77.6% (R9, R10); Table 1 reports 72%–79% across its CIFAR10 model and training-set conditions (R1–R8). Random-label performance was not tested.
